ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1 meter in length. It is olive-brown with a pale, dark-edged lateral stripe. Key features include a narrow head, large eyes, and a distinctively elongated, whip-like tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Platyceps gracilis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged white stripe running along the side of its head and neck, unlike similar local racers.
ai.habitat: The Graceful Racer inhabits dry, open deciduous forests and scrublands, typically found at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Graceful Racer is a highly active, diurnal snake that hunts during the day, using its slender build and speed to forage for small lizards among rocks and vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Platyceps gracilis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Platyceps gracilis* is found in the arid and semi-arid regions of northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and parts of Haryana and Punjab.
